clue.text: Item that's thrust from artist on jetty

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
a pier is a jetty projecting into the sea

explanation.surface: Something is pushed off a painter standing on a landing stage.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places RA above PIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender sword is used for thrusting rather than slashing, so it is an item that is thrust.

clue.text: Duke with natural inclination to avoid North once? That's clear

indicators.note: to avoid says the letter for North is kept out of the word, here only once

parts.note: an instinct is a natural inclination
N is the compass abbreviation for North

explanation.surface: A query about whether a duke's leanings once steered him away from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for natural inclination holds two Ns; 'once' says only one goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something distinct is plainly marked and easy to make out, a synonym of clear.

clue.text: Poser with talent, suspect character

parts.note: a poser is a puzzling question
talent is ability

explanation.surface: A gifted show-off turns out to be a dodgy individual.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of suspect character means being open to doubt, which is what the abstract noun describes.

clue.text: Dining area with time for communication

parts.note: a mess is where service personnel eat
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A canteen plus an era somehow add up to a note.
explanation.definitionFit: A note or letter sent to someone is a communication.

clue.text: Occasion when crosses are placed countrywide?

definitions.text: Occasion when crosses are placed countrywide?

parts.words: Occasion when crosses are placed countrywide?
parts.note: voters across the whole nation mark Xs on ballot papers on this day

explanation.surface: Sounds like a nationwide day of putting up crucifixes or memorials.
explanation.definitionFit: On a national polling day every voter marks a cross beside a candidate's name.

clue.text: District with church that's roughly normal?

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
the suffix -ish means roughly, as in 'sixish'

explanation.surface: A query whether a district with a church is fairly ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly normal' reads as 'par-ish', with the suffix after PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A local administrative district served by its own church and priest.

clue.text: Dogs, maybe, in section of supermarket heard

indicators.note: heard says the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: an aisle is a row between shelves in a supermarket

explanation.surface: Dogs wandering in a supermarket aisle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Dogs is a district in London's Docklands, so 'Dogs' is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Dogs in east London is one example of an island name.

clue.text: Some admired a lively artist

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people admired a vivacious painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dalí was a Spanish surrealist painter, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Contemplation after minute's gone in exercise

indicators.note: gone says the minute's letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: to muse is to ponder, and a muse is a fit of contemplation
M is the abbreviation for minute; the 's stands for 'has'

explanation.surface: Meditation once a minute has passed during a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a right or power is to employ it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Pass drinks hidden in middle of beer

indicators.note: hidden in puts the drinking word inside the letters taken from beer
middle of takes the central letters of the word beer

parts.note: an animal laps when it drinks with its tongue

explanation.surface: Someone passes on drinks concealed in a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' looks like a noun but works as the verb meaning to go by.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to pass or go by, a straight synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Opening? It has developed around university

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters surround the university letter
developed says the letters of it has are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: An opening has grown up around a campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' turns IT HAS into HIATS, which goes around U.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap or break in a sequence is an opening, the original sense of the Latin word.

clue.text: Object in collection, remarkable type

definitions.meaning: an item kept as an example in a museum or scientific collection
a notable person, as in 'a fine example of a man'

explanation.surface: A striking item in a museum display.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: an example item kept for study, and colloquially a person of remarkable kind.

clue.text: Source of legitimacy in post?

parts.note: a device that stamps envelopes to show postage has been paid, making them valid mail

explanation.surface: Sounds like asking what gives someone authority in their job.
explanation.definitionFit: Envelopes stamped by this office device count as paid, so it validates mail.

clue.text: Sister, not a person appearing in speech

indicators.note: appearing in speech says the word is taken as it is spoken

parts.note: none means not one person, nobody

explanation.surface: A nun says no one is present.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman in a religious order is called Sister, the title for a member of a convent.

clue.text: Set of bars showing good value

parts.note: a rating is an assessed value

explanation.surface: A prison window grille offers good value.
explanation.definitionFit: A framework of parallel bars over a drain or window is a grille.

clue.text: One starts in regularly undertaken tasks

definitions.text: One starts in regularly undertaken tasks

indicators.note: starts says the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone begins a routine of chores.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a monotonous routine one can get stuck in, while 'starts' takes the first letters of the last three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull routine of repeated chores is something one gets stuck in, the figurative groove.

clue.text: Lie back in park, beside path

indicators.note: beside says the path word sits next to the park word

parts.note: rec, short for recreation ground, is a British word for a public park
a line is a path or route

explanation.surface: Someone stretches out in a park next to a footpath.
explanation.definitionFit: To lean or lie back in a relaxed position is a synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Free period in company supplying many lines in story

indicators.note: the second in places the whole inside the word for a fib

parts.note: a story can be a lie, a fib

indicators.note: in puts the period inside the company letters

parts.note: BT, British Telecom, supplies telephone lines in the UK
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A firm takes a break from producing a script.
explanation.walkthrough: BT is British Telecom, the UK phone company that supplies telephone lines.
explanation.definitionFit: To set someone at liberty is to free them, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Give up trick with top player, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the pieces are taken by their sound

parts.note: con is a trick and a seed is a top-ranked player, so the phrase sounds like con seed

explanation.surface: A tennis player gives up against a top seed.
explanation.walkthrough: A seed is a highly ranked player in a tennis tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit defeat or yield a point is to give up.

clue.text: Devise block to berserk development finally in well-to-do area

indicators.note: devise says the letters are reworked into something new
finally takes the last letter of the word development

explanation.surface: Instruction to plan a block development in a smart neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devise' rearranges BLOCK TO BERSERK; 'development finally' adds T at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A commuter belt of affluent suburbs where finance people live, an idiom for a wealthy area.

clue.text: Appeal lies in more than 50 per cent of sport for reviewer

indicators.note: lies in says the appeal word sits inside the shortened sport
more than half of the seven letters of the sport are kept: the opening four

parts.note: cricket is a bat-and-ball sport
it is a dated term for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Charm is found in most of a sport, per a reviewer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' meaning sex appeal is old-fashioned slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A reviewer judges books, films or plays, which is what this person does.

clue.text: Ring, conceivably, as bedridden?

indicators.note: conceivably says the letters could be arranged differently

parts.note: to dial up is to ring someone on the telephone

explanation.surface: A query whether someone confined to bed might ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first four letters of DIAL UP actually move: DIAL becomes LAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone confined to bed by illness is out of action, an idiom for being bedridden.

clue.text: Scoundrel sick to get bill for car

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man
ill means sick
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A rogue feels queasy on receiving the invoice for his vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: An American luxury make of motor vehicle, an example of a car.

clue.text: Neighbour taking instrument up

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tuba is a brass instrument

explanation.surface: A neighbour carries an instrument upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a verb: to adjoin or border something, as a neighbouring property does.

clue.text: Swollen gut? I'd fancy that's about right

indicators.note: that's about says the rearranged letters surround the right letter
fancy says the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the contraction I'd gives the letters I and D

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a bloated stomach is about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' turns GUT into TUG, which goes around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Distended or swollen with fluid; also used of pompous, inflated prose.

clue.text: One with barely seen family jewels?

definitions.text: One with barely seen family jewels?

parts.words: One with barely seen family jewels?
parts.note: family jewels is slang for male genitals, which are seen bare by someone who goes unclothed

explanation.surface: Seems to describe an heir whose heirlooms are rarely on display.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes unclothed, so private parts are on show 'barely', with no covering.

clue.text: Pair from union in function

indicators.note: in places the union letter inside the party word

parts.note: a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: A couple emerges from a trade union event.
explanation.definitionFit: Two performers working together are a duet act, a synonym for a pair.

clue.text: Solicitor disclosed after beginning of trial

indicators.note: after says the disclosed word comes behind that letter
beginning of takes the first letter of the word trial

parts.note: out means revealed or made public

explanation.surface: A lawyer revealed something once a trial began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' looks like the legal profession but here means someone who solicits custom.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket seller or hawker who pesters people for business is one who solicits.
